positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Owner of WhatsApp Web release processes serving over 250 million active users.
Performance and reliability champion at WhatsApp.
No major incidents or outages during my tenure.

Web Client Dev Infra (most recent)
     Established ownership over WhatsApp Web's release processes with new monitoring, detection, and alerting capabilities.  Prevented multiple major regressions.  Promoted to senior engineer.
     Led a team transformation from bi-weekly releases off a branch to continuous daily releases off of `main`.  This supported a multi-year migration from the WhatsApp Git repo to Meta’s Mercurial based mono-repo and associated release processes.  Production deployment now happens every few hours.
     Designed and implemented WhatsApp Web’s client versioning and upgrade strategy for the above migration.  Supported developer workflows for bug detection and triage including contingency procedures for rollback.

Performance, Reliability, Efficiency
     Implemented QPL (Quick Performance Logging) for WhatsApp Web.  Fostered adoption through a developer API and wiki along with awareness efforts.  The team leveraged QPL to identify performance gaps and improve startup times by 20%.

Web Dev Infra
      Independently owned Web's Erlang code and server deployments known as 'webd', which hosted tens of millions of concurrent users.  Performed infrastructure upgrades via draining clusters/regions, pushing updates, and then restoring traffic. 

Summer Intern Manager
SEV Review Coordinator
 Owner and moderator of the WhatsApp Companion organization’s bi-weekly retrospective on recent incidents (SEVs).  
Treehugger, Meta release steward
 Member of on-call rotation responsible for Meta’s continuous release process and shipping the majority of Meta’s ecosystem.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
First developer and second employee to join the company.  Helped facilitate the early culture and eventual growth to over 100 employees

Full Stack Developer, PFO (Plan Field Operations), Monsanto/Bayer (client)
      `PFO` (Plan Field Operations), was a flagship product at Monsanto.  PFO had over 3000 internal users and hosted the millions of geospatial records and APIs necessary to support scientific trials, commercial seed production, and payments to farmers.
     I led a large multi-year migration of PFO systems.  First we migrated existing services away from internal hosting and onto AWS.  Following that we planned a full migration of all geospatial systems and data storage away from Esri (an expensive proprietary platform) to Geoserver (a free open source alternative).  The resulting effort spanned two years and included multiple data migrations along with the creation of a new UI (JS/React) and associated APIs (NodeJS/Elasticsearch) for querying, interacting with, and modifying Geoserver data. During transition we supported the legacy system and the new system concurrently through optimistic dual data writes (legacy was source of truth) and occasional syncs.  After the new version of PFO was fully operational legacy systems were deprecated.  We completed the largest geospatial product launch in Monsanto's history.

Lunch-and-Learn Coordinator
 Scheduled, promoted, provided lunch, and video recorded over 25 sessions.
Mentor, Hours With Experts
 Established and mentored the inaugural 10 week JS course, open to the community.
Tickled Pink Award Winner                                         
 https://insights.1904labs.com/blog/2018-05-22-jared-parker-is-awarded-1904labs-second-tickled-pink-award
St Patrick Center Irish Open and Gala Ambassador                                                                     
Organized annual support and sponsorship for St Patrick Center in St Louis.
